commit_message:
[Stream] Fix ARC double-dealloca of aliased control-flow results (#24841)

The ARC pass emitted multiple deallocations for possibly aliasing
results pointing to the same buffer, leading to double-deallocation
and/or deallocation/usage race.

ARC assumed that each result of a control-flow op is a distinct buffer,
unless the values yielded into two results resolve to the same buffer
through their tied-value chain. But a (nested) control-flow op's result
is defined by a control-flow op, which is not tied to anything, since it
may hold a different yielded value on each path. The analysis then
treated both as separate buffers.

The fix collects the tied-value chain for each path. A yielded value
thus resolves to the set of allocations it
may hold. If there is an overlap, the values may alias.


Think the pass might need a closer look/some refactoring at some point -
the fix is just patching this up.

Co-Authored-By: Claude

Integrate LLVM to llvm/llvm-project@c22aa41c054e

Carries a revert of 90cebef14116 (MemCpyOpt forms llvm.memset without a
libcall check): X86 lowers a 1856-byte memset in a no-builtins dispatch to a
memset libcall the -nostdlib embedded link cannot resolve.

* 40d4395bb229, 65b48e45ea94, b570e2aa0aa4: Arith header no longer transitive.
* 3b99e79991be, 70f5696eaf02, 80164074c01f, f7dd24bbe0e9: Linalg unary and
  binary named ops removed; tests use linalg.elementwise <kind>.
* 2eb384fccbf8: generalizeNamedOp returns FailureOr<LinalgOp>.
* 173a02c755bf: LLVM dialect strict property assembly format in CHECK lines.
* fc696f791e06: aggregate builders with mixed attributes are deprecated and
  fatal under Bazel's -Werror; call sites use typed builders, copy the source
  op's properties, or build through OperationState.

commit_message:
[Stream] Fix ARC double-dealloca of aliased control-flow results (#24841)

The ARC pass emitted multiple deallocations for possibly aliasing
results pointing to the same buffer, leading to double-deallocation
and/or deallocation/usage race.

ARC assumed that each result of a control-flow op is a distinct buffer,
unless the values yielded into two results resolve to the same buffer
through their tied-value chain. But a (nested) control-flow op's result
is defined by a control-flow op, which is not tied to anything, since it
may hold a different yielded value on each path. The analysis then
treated both as separate buffers.

The fix collects the tied-value chain for each path. A yielded value
thus resolves to the set of allocations it
may hold. If there is an overlap, the values may alias.


Think the pass might need a closer look/some refactoring at some point -
the fix is just patching this up.

Co-Authored-By: Claude

---------

commit_message:
[Stream] Fix ARC double-dealloca of aliased control-flow results (#24841)

The ARC pass emitted multiple deallocations for possibly aliasing
results pointing to the same buffer, leading to double-deallocation
and/or deallocation/usage race.

ARC assumed that each result of a control-flow op is a distinct buffer,
unless the values yielded into two results resolve to the same buffer
through their tied-value chain. But a (nested) control-flow op's result
is defined by a control-flow op, which is not tied to anything, since it
may hold a different yielded value on each path. The analysis then
treated both as separate buffers.

The fix collects the tied-value chain for each path. A yielded value
thus resolves to the set of allocations it
may hold. If there is an overlap, the values may alias.


Think the pass might need a closer look/some refactoring at some point -
the fix is just patching this up.

commit_message: [LinalgExt] Add affine quantization and dequantization ops (#24901) Adds `iree_linalg_ext.quantize_affine` and `iree_linalg_ext.dequantize_affine` to represent QDQ directly in LinalgExt, preserving quantization parameters for subsequent compiler transformations. Independent indexing maps for the input, scale, zero point, and output express per-tensor, per-channel, and blockwise quantization. The ops support optional zero points, explicit storage and zero-point signedness, and arithmetic in the scale's element type. Quantization rounds ties to even and clamps to the specified storage range. Includes operation verification, shape reification, and decomposition into elementwise Linalg generics. Dispatch creation decomposes remaining QDQ ops before fusion, allowing earlier optimizations to consume the explicit quantization representation. commit_message:
[GlobalOptimization] Rewrite QDQ contractions into integer math

Rewrite contractions over affine-dequantized operands as integer
contractions with zero-point corrections and a scaling epilogue:

  C = sA*sB*(D - zB*RA - zA*RB + N*zA*zB)

Compose storage and parameter maps into contraction coordinates. Reduce
in integer arithmetic where parameters are invariant; retain the other
reduction dimensions as partial results for the floating-point epilogue.
Windowed operand sums use the same access expressions as the
contraction.

Match only plain multiply-add bodies with zero initialization. Require
positive static integer reduction extents and prove that all integer
intermediates fit in signed i32 using the separate storage and zero-
point ranges. Unsupported cases retain the original computation.

Apply corrections before converting to float. Evaluate scaling and
blockwise accumulation in at least f32, preserving wider scale and
output types, and narrow only the final result. Reassociation changes
rounding. Enable the rewrite by default; it can be disabled with
--iree-global-opt-enable-qdq-to-integer-math=false.

Cover the rewrite with three compiler regression files: correction terms
and widening, indexing maps and result shapes, and the contractions the
rewrite declines. Add CPU execution checks for blockwise and convolution
zero-point corrections alongside the original QDQ path.

commit_message:
[LinalgExt] Drop a provably zero zero_point from the quantization ops

A dequantize whose zero point is zero is symmetric, and every consumer
benefits from seeing it that way: the QDQ to integer rewrite skips a
whole correction term, and the decomposition skips a subtraction.

Quantizers spell a symmetric zero point as a splat, as an explicit
tensor of zeros, or, once the model is frozen, as a resource blob whose
bytes live outside the attribute. isKnownZero answers a splat from its
one stored element and everything else from raw bytes: for an integer
tensor, all bytes zero is equivalent to all elements zero whatever the
width and packing, so no element is materialized as an APInt and the
resource case needs no per width decoding. Padding bytes can only make
the answer a conservative false.

The element type is not rechecked. The only caller passes a zero_point
the op verifier has already established to be an integer.

zero_point is the only optional operand, so the ops carry no operand
segment attribute and the drop is an in place mutation: clear the
operand, drop its indexing map, remove zp_unsigned. Everything else the
op carries is preserved by construction rather than by an attribute
copy that would have to be revisited whenever an attribute is added.

[GlobalOptimization] Propagate QDQ through layout operations

Move quantize operations toward real-valued producers and dequantize
operations toward contraction consumers before rewriting contractions to
integer math.

Reuse reshape expansion and unit-dimension folding for affine QDQ
operations. Handle transpose and zero-pad consumers using explicit
legality checks.

commit_message:
[Torch] Preserve PT2E quantization as LinalgExt ops

Convert the typed PT2E per-tensor and per-channel quantize and
dequantize operations before Torch-to-Linalg expands them. This keeps
affine parameter maps, ranges, and signedness available to later QDQ
optimizations.

Leave operations with dynamic or incompatible metadata for the
existing torch-mlir lowering.

commit_message:
[Runtime] Fix sysfs incorrect topology (#24828)

Fixes incorrect topology creation by using the `node/node<N>/cpulist` to
deduce the NUMA nodes and CPU relation instead of cluster or package ids
which have different meanings.
As far as I can tell, the node_id is intended to always be the NUMA node
id, since this is later used to bind memory to a specific NUMA node.

- Fixed cluster/numa node confusion
- Fixed ignored file read errors
- Fixed ignored path length errors
- Added a testing path injection
- Added tests

Fixes https://github.com/iree-org/iree/issues/24761

for sysfs knowledge)
